newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian blue chips gain in more active trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian blue chips gain in more active trade.

text.p: Lithuanian blue chips gained in higher trade on Tuesday as investors returned to the market, dealers said.
The official list index, launched on Monday, crept up by 5.02 points to 1,005.2.
Dealers said investors had digested the results of a spate of recent shareholders' meetings and were returning to the market.
Four blue chips are currently on the official list: cardboard producer Medienos Plaushas, Rokishkis Cheese, Vilniaus Bank and Hermis Bank.
"The official list should increase foreign interest in the market, especially since the companies which make the list are the most transparent," one London-based equities analyst told Reuters.
The Litin A index, which tracks the bourse's 35 most acvtive companies, rose by 10.01 points to 2,572.18, while the Litin G index dipped by 45.66 points to 2,227.91.
Overall central market volume was over 2.15 million litas compared with just 512,000 litas on Monday while block trades turned over almost 16 million litas.
Hermis Bank was by far the most active listing in trade of 1.13 million litas. Its price advanced to 195.00 litas from 191.00 litas.
The bank earlier reported that its 1Q net profit was 9.3 million litas versus 4.4 million litas for the same period last year.
